successors.note: 26 August 1303: "Alauddin entered the fort" and assigned Chittor to his son Khizr Khan.

The junior Sisodia branch "established the Sisodia Rajput dynasty" and ruled Mewar to 1948 (infobox); its Hammir Singh held Chittor after the death of Maladeva "around 1321" (Peter Jackson: Delhi governors held it into the Tughluq period). Needs its own dossier.

capitals.name: Nagahrada (Nagda) / Aghata (Ahar)
capitals.note: Lead: capitals Nagahrada (Nagda) and Aghata (Ahar); infobox "Seat: Ahar; Nagda; Chittor". "Towards the end of the 10th century, Ahar became the second capital of the Guhilas." Nagda (about 24.6N 73.8E) and Ahar (24.6N 73.7E) lie a few km from Udaipur; coordinates are approximate. Review fix 2026-10-19: this seat stays to 1212, because Chittor was not Guhila from c. 975 to 1213 in this dossier.

capitals.name: Chitrakuta (Chittorgarh)
capitals.note: The senior branch "ruled from Chitrakuta (modern Chittorgarh)"; the page dates neither the first use nor the shift (the earliest Guhila inscription found at Chittor "is from Tejasimha's reign"). Chittor was Paramara and then Chaulukya ("By 1151 ... Kumarapala"), so the seat can only be Chittor after the Guhilas regained it: 1213 is the placeholder year of that return. Review fix 2026-10-19: was 1151.

correction.text: Nagahrada (Nagda) and Aghata (Ahar), the early Guhila seats in Mewar (Medapata)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Mewar row). Infobox "Founded: 566"; Majumdar places Guhadatta "in the 5th century CE", Somani "somewhere before the first quarter of the 6th century", so 566 is the infobox's, not a certain date. The page names Nagda and Ahar as the early seats and gives no area; the 60 km radius round Udaipur is the researcher's reading of the first Guhila country.

New keyframe. "Bappa Rawal established the Mewar Kingdom in 728 CE" (Ekalinga Mahatmya) and "captured famous Chitrakuta (Chittor Fort) from the mlechchhas" (undated; the Moris ruled Chittor when the Arabs invaded north-western India around 725 CE). The page itself warns that Bappa Rawal "wrongly came to be regarded as the founder" and may be an epithet. Pratihara feudatories: "The Guhila kings initially ruled as feudatories of the Pratiharas during the 8th and the 9th century", and "assumed sovereignty in the 10th century" (Guhila page, re-read 2026-10-19). All of this shape lies inside gurjara-pratihara-dynasty's shapes, so the lighter vassal tint belongs to gurjara-pratihara-dynasty: it should carry vassal_start (c. 750, the page says only 'the 8th century') and vassal_end (c. 900) with counterpart guhilas-of-mewar; the Guhila dossier cannot record the suzerain's side. Review fix 2026-10-19: the shape now ends in 974; the Paramara conquest of eastern Mewar and Chittorgarh follows (next keyframe).

correction.text: Nagahrada (Nagda) and Aghata (Ahar), western Mewar: after Munja the Paramaras held "the eastern part of Mewar, including Chittorgarh"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review fix 2026-10-19; replaces the former 1151-1212 shape 'Mewar minus Chittor'). "In the later 10th century, the Paramara king Munja defeated the elephant forces of the Guhilas and plundered their capital Ahar. As a result of this victory, the Paramaras gained control of the eastern part of Mewar, including Chittorgarh." The year 975 is a bridge (the page says 'later 10th century'; inscriptions of Naravahana 971 and Shaktikumara 977 at Atpur show the Guhilas still at Ahar). The shape is western Mewar, the 60 km disc round Nagda and Ahar, which is the part of the Mewar region the page leaves to the Guhilas (the eastern part is the same region the 728 gain adds). Chittor then passes from the Paramaras to the Chaulukyas: "By 1151, Chittor was under the control of the Chaulukya king Kumarapala" (a Paramara-to-Chaulukya change, not a Guhila loss; the Chittorgarh page is silent on all of it). Kirtipala of Naddula ousted Samantasimha from Mewar (probably 1171-1179) and "By 1182" Kumarasimha "regained the control of his ancestral kingdom by appeasing the Chaulukya king Bhima II": read here as the western core, with no change of shape (the interlude is a few undated years). The page does not say when or from whom the Guhilas regained Chittor; the next keyframe assumes 1213. Overlap: the neighbours' shapes (paramara-dynasty 1018-1055, chaulukya-dynasty 1136-1201) still contain parts of this disc; see the notes.

New keyframe. "During the reign of Jaitrasimha (r. c. 1213-1252), the Guhilas achieved a high political status"; Ratnasimha was in Chittor in 1303 (siege page). The Jaitrasimha page gives no boundary and names Naddula, Kottadaka and Arthuna only as places of his campaigns. Chittor and the eastern part of Mewar return to the Guhilas by the end of the previous span; Chittorgarh page (opened 2026-10-19): silent on who held Chittor in 1213 and on the date; it says only that "some historians doubt" the Guhilas held Chittor before the reign of Allata.

region.text: Nagahrada (Nagda) and Aghata (Ahar), the early Guhila seats in Mewar (Medapata)

ledger.note: 566: the Guhila dynasty of Medapata. Infobox "Founded: 566"; the page cautions that Guhadatta is placed "in the 5th century CE" (Majumdar) or "somewhere before the first quarter of the 6th century" (Somani).

region.text: Chitrakuta (Chittor Fort) and the eastern Mewar region

ledger.note: 728: Bappa Rawal sits on the throne of Chitor. "Bappa Rawal established the Mewar Kingdom in 728 CE" and "captured famous Chitrakuta (Chittor Fort) from the mlechchhas"; the capture itself is undated. The page offers Somani's theory that he captured "the eastern parts of Mewar region" while helping the Pratiharas. The Guhilas held this land as Pratihara feudatories (see the first keyframe's note).

region.text: the eastern part of Mewar, including Chittorgarh

ledger.note: c. 975 (bridge): Munja takes eastern Mewar. "As a result of this victory, the Paramaras gained control of the eastern part of Mewar, including Chittorgarh" (after Munja "defeated the elephant forces of the Guhilas" and "plundered their capital Ahar"). The page dates it only to the later 10th century; the year is the researcher's bridge. paramara-dynasty should carry the matching gain.

region.text: Chittor and the eastern part of Mewar

ledger.note: 1213 (bridge): Chittor and eastern Mewar are again Guhila by the end of this span. The Jaitrasimha page (r. c. 1213-1252) gives no recapture date; the Guhilas "achieved a high political status" in his reign and Ratnasimha defended Chittor in 1303. Chittor was Chaulukya by 1151 (Kumarapala, Guhila page); the Chittorgarh page (opened 2026-10-19 for this question) names no holder in the 12th-13th centuries and no recapture, so the taker stays unknown. Review fix fx-33 (2026-11-01): the Chaulukya dynasty page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaulukya_dynasty) names the counterpart: the Guhilas of Medapata 'also rebelled against Bhima sometime between 1207 and 1227 CE, and declared their independence'. No year inside the window; 1213 stays the bridge. The loss is mirrored in chaulukya-dynasty ledger 24 for the 60 Mewar cells of the Chaulukya shape.

26 August 1303: Alauddin Khalji takes Chittor. "On 26 August 1303, Alauddin entered the fort"; the defender was "the Guhila king Ratnasimha" and the fort was assigned to Khizr Khan and renamed "Khizrabad".

August 1303: the Rawal branch ends. "The Rawal branch ended when Ratnasiṃha was defeated by Alauddin Khalji in the Siege of Chittorgarh (1303)"; infobox "Deposition 26 August 1303 (main branch)". The Sisodia branch carried on and held Chittor after "around 1321".

wars.name: Paramara conquest of eastern Mewar
wars.outcome: Munja "defeated the elephant forces of the Guhilas" and "plundered their capital Ahar"; the Paramaras gained the eastern part of Mewar including Chittorgarh. The defeated Guhila ruler (Naravahana or Shaktikumara) "took shelter with Dhavala, the Rashtrakuta ruler of Hastikundi".
wars.note: Later 10th century on the page; 975 is a bridge year.

wars.name: Iltutmish's invasion of Mewar
wars.outcome: "Early in his reign, the Delhi Sultanate ruler Iltutmish invaded Mewar, and destroyed Nagada"; no territorial change is named.
wars.note: The page gives no year; the span is Jaitrasimha's reign. The Bhutala battle is listed in the infobox without date or result.

wars.name: Siege of Chittorgarh (1303)
wars.outcome: The siege ran from 28 January to 26 August 1303; Alauddin Khalji captured Chittor and gave it to his son Khizr Khan.
wars.note: Later control: Hammir Singh of the Sisodia branch after Maladeva's death "around 1321"; Peter Jackson argues Delhi governors still held it under the first two Tughluqs.

certainty.note: No frontier is given on any page; Mewar (Medapata) and Chittor are the only places the pages place.

sources.note: 728 and the capture of Chitrakuta; historicity warnings.

notes: Cliopatria has no Mewar or Guhila row. Five pages (four, plus the Chittorgarh page opened for the review); the Guhila article gives almost no dated territory. Review fixes 2026-10-19: (1) the Paramara conquest of eastern Mewar with Chittorgarh under Munja (page: 'later 10th century') is now a loss c. 975, confidence 1, to paramara-dynasty (which should carry the matching gain; neither it nor chaulukya-dynasty names the Guhilas); the shape from 975 to 1212 is western Mewar only (60 km round Udaipur: Nagda and Ahar), and the 1151 loss to the Chaulukyas is dropped because the 1151 change is Paramara to Chaulukya (Guhila page: 'By 1151, Chittor was under the control of the Chaulukya king Kumarapala'; chaulukya-dynasty already shows Chittor Chaulukya by 1151). (2) The capital is Nagda/Ahar to 1212 and Chittor from 1213 (the page names no move; 1213 is the placeholder year of the return). (3) Pratihara feudatory status in the 8th and 9th century cannot be recorded here (the vassal events belong to the suzerain): gurjara-pratihara-dynasty should add vassal_start c. 750 and vassal_end c. 900 with counterpart guhilas-of-mewar; the first keyframe says so. Disagreements: none with the reviewer. Not drawn: the interlude of Kirtipala's ouster of Samantasimha (probably 1171-1179) and Kumarasimha's recovery 'by 1182' by appeasing Bhima II (no territory named; the western core is kept), and a possible Chaulukya overlordship from 1182 to the revolt of 1207-1227 that chaulukya-dynasty cites (the Guhila page does not describe that revolt). chaulukya-dynasty's 1210 Cliopatria shape still holds 60 cells of Mewar, which overlap the western core drawn here. Still open: when and from whom Chittor returned before 1213 (Guhila, Jaitrasimha and Chittorgarh pages are silent), the dates of Pratihara suzerainty, the Rashtrakuta refuge (Dhavala of Hastikundi) and Iltutmish's destruction of Nagda. The dossier ends with the Rawal branch (August 1303); the Sisodia line that held Mewar to 1948 needs its own dossier under kingdom-of-mewar (dynasty change inside one state, so the colour should continue). Gazetteer lacks Nagda, Ahar. Counterparts needing a dossier: kingdom-of-mewar (1303..1948). Grid check 2026-10-19 of the western core (46 cells) against the neighbours' keyframes: paramara-dynasty 1018-1055 holds 44 of them (Bhoja shape reaching Chittor), 1136-1187 holds 16; chaulukya-dynasty 1136-1201 holds 30; the page-based reading here (Guhilas keep Nagda and Ahar) therefore overlaps those Cliopatria-derived shapes, and the neighbours' dossiers should decide.
